beats.title: The Need for Second-Order Derivatives in a GPU Neural Network Library
beats.body: tiny-cuda-nn lacked support for second-order (higher-order) derivatives, which are required for certain optimization techniques such as backpropagating through gradient computations. A contributor stepped in to add this capability, initially scoped only to the grid encoding module and only for specific derivative directions.

beats.title: Partial vs. Complete Coverage: How Far Should the Initial Contribution Go?
beats.body: The contributor could ship a narrowly scoped but correct and well-tested implementation covering only the grid encoding, or attempt broader coverage across all modules. Expanding scope risks introducing bugs and delays, while a partial implementation may leave users of other modules without the feature they need.

beats.title: Position A — ventusff
beats.body: ventusff argued for iterative, incremental delivery: ship a correct partial implementation first, then extend it. After reviewer feedback, they went further than originally planned and added an additional derivative direction, demonstrating that a well-scoped starting point can organically grow without sacrificing quality.
beats.author: ventusff

beats.title: Position B — Tom94
beats.body: Tom94 emphasized code quality, documentation, and alignment with the project's evolving conventions as prerequisites for merging. He also raised the value of including test scripts in the repository to guard against future regressions, treating long-term maintainability as equally important as the new functionality itself.
beats.author: Tom94

beats.question: Given the tradeoff between shipping partial but high-quality support now versus waiting for complete coverage across all modules, what would you decide and why?
